os-dev-report

**Verdict: leave all five. No code change, no PR.** The shape census is correct — I re-derived it and it matches this card row for row — but the cost the card deliberately left unmeasured is, for every one of the five rows, **between 0.03 ms and 0.11 ms against a 10 000 ms budget**. Every row is already paid outside the clock by the file's own module-top imports.

## Measurement rig, and its control

Each target test file was instrumented in place (a timing IIFE wrapped around every `await import` site of the specifier), then run **alone in its own vitest invocation** so no sibling file had pre-warmed Vite's transform cache — the coldest realistic condition, colder than CI, which runs all 98 files together. Restore under `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths; every file verified back at its HEAD blob.

**The control fires, hard.** `durability-swallow-repair.test.ts` / `./admin-import-users.js` — the site PR #15914 fixes, still unfixed on `main`, so it is measurable here as a positive control in the same rig:

```
PROBE15916|durability-swallow-repair.test.ts|./admin-import-users.js|#1|3086.379
PROBE15916|durability-swallow-repair.test.ts|./admin-import-users.js|#2|0.043
PROBE15916|durability-swallow-repair.test.ts|./admin-import-users.js|#3|0.034
```

3086.379 ms cold, two warm siblings at 0.04 ms — reproducing PR #15914's 3299.6 ms / 0.014 ms to within 7 % on a shared box. So a sub-millisecond reading elsewhere in this rig is a measurement, not a blind spot.

## Per-row result

`in-file` is what the first-payer case actually pays. `vacuum` is the same specifier loaded by a throwaway probe importing nothing else — the full cold graph, for contrast.

| file | specifier | first payer | in-file cold | vacuum cold | absorbed at module top |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `admin-user-endpoints.test.ts` | `./admin-user-endpoints.js` | it@74 | **0.097 ms** | 591.7 ms | yes — same specifier already imported at `:11` |
| `auth-manager.test.ts` | `better-auth/api` | it@2209 | **0.045 ms** | 215.8 ms | yes — via the module-top graph |
| `auth-manager.test.ts` | `./rate-limit-storage.js` | it@2358 | **0.067 ms** | 52.7 ms | yes — via the module-top graph |
| `admin-impersonate-endpoint.test.ts` | `better-auth` | it@358 | **0.082 ms** | 307.9 ms | yes — via the module-top graph |
| `managed-extension-fields.test.ts` | `better-auth/plugins` | it@1046 | **0.108 ms** | 297.3 ms | yes — same specifier already imported at `:105` |
| *(control)* `durability-swallow-repair.test.ts` | `./admin-import-users.js` | it@673 | **3086.379 ms** | **10064.1 ms** | **no** |

The control's vacuum figure is the headline: `./admin-import-users.js` costs **10 064 ms to load with nothing else resident — it exceeds the entire 10 000 ms testTimeout on its own.** That is why it flaked six times. The worst card row is **0.108 ms**, i.e. 0.0011 % of budget, a load-tolerance of about 92 600x before it could red. The spread between the control and the worst card row is roughly **28 000x in-file**.

**Three of the five rows would be actively wrong to hoist.** `admin-user-endpoints.test.ts:11`, `managed-extension-fields.test.ts:105` and (see below) `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts:103` already carry a module-top static import of *the very specifier* the `it()` body re-imports. Hoisting there does not relocate a load — it adds a second module-top import of a module the file already imports. These `await import` calls are stylistic redundancy, not a timeout hazard.

## The two single-sibling rows, answered explicitly

`admin-impersonate-endpoint.test.ts` (`better-auth`, 0.082 ms) and `managed-extension-fields.test.ts` (`better-auth/plugins`, 0.108 ms): **leave both.** They had no warm sibling to contrast against, so the rig contrasts them against the vacuum figure instead — 307.9 ms and 297.3 ms of graph, of which the case pays 0.08 and 0.11 ms because the file's module-top imports already resident it. This is a measured verdict, not a default.

## Coverage safety, re-established per file

Checked per file rather than assumed. `vi.mock` / `vi.doMock` / `vi.resetModules` / `vi.unmock` counts: `admin-user-endpoints.test.ts` 0/0/0/0, `admin-impersonate-endpoint.test.ts` 0/0/0/0, `managed-extension-fields.test.ts` 0/0/0/0, `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts` 0/0/0/0.

`auth-manager.test.ts` (4 796 lines) is the exception the card flagged and it does carry **six `vi.mock` calls** — `better-auth` and five `better-auth/plugins/*` subpaths. Neither of its two dynamic specifiers is among them: `better-auth/api` and `./rate-limit-storage.js` are unmocked, and both sites merely destructure a function (`isAPIError`, `createLazyCounterStore`) with no dependence on mock state established in a hook. So a hoist would have been safe there — it is simply not worth doing. Worth recording that `vi.mock('better-auth', ...)` means that file's module-top `better-auth` import loads the mock, so `better-auth/api` is genuinely unwarmed by it; the 0.045 ms comes from elsewhere in the module-top graph.

## Census re-derivation — one confirmation and one gap

Re-derived at `e581457ba` with a brace-tracking scanner that **masks comments** via a tokenizer skipping strings, templates and regex literals.

- **The disclosed limitation is exactly as disclosed.** Masking removes exactly one site and nothing else: `rate-limit-storage-isolation.test.ts:128`, specifier `x`, in prose. Totals 24 to 23; module-scope bucket 3 to 2; the clocked bucket is unchanged at 21, so the finding set never contained it. The other two module-scope sites (`auth-email-locale.test.ts:89`, `verification-email-failure-propagation.test.ts:54`) are confirmed compliant.
- **The firing control is reproduced**: `credential-at-rest-posture.test.ts` / `@better-auth/scim` / it@336 is detected *with* its explicit `60_000`.
- All five finding rows reproduce exactly — same file, same specifier, same first-payer line, same site counts.

**Gap: the census misses a sixth row.** `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts` / `better-auth/plugins/jwt`, first payer **it@671**, 2 sites, no explicit timeout — the same shape, in the finding population, absent from the table. It is not a new file: it exists at `6b3c135fe` and the only file added since is `membership-ended-session.test.ts` (which has no dynamic imports). The cause is mechanical and worth recording for anyone re-running this sweep: that site is written with the specifier on **its own line**, so a single-line `await import('...')` regex cannot see it. A pattern allowing whitespace across newlines finds it. This makes the true pre-fix package total **24 sites unmasked / 23 masked**, not 22.

I measured the sixth row too: **0.085 ms in-file**, 200.7 ms vacuum, and `better-auth/plugins/jwt` is already statically imported at `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts:103`. Same verdict — leave it. So the gap changes the census arithmetic but leaves no unaddressed work behind it, which is why I am recording it here rather than filing a card.

## Does this let #15603 close?

**It removes the objection that kept it open, but it is not itself sufficient — and the ruling is the maintainer's.** PR #15914's rationale for striking the `Fixes` line was that five sites of identical shape remained unmeasured and the 69x spread made cheap-or-expensive unknowable. Those five are now measured, plus a sixth, and all six are between 0.03 ms and 0.11 ms — they cannot contribute to a shard-level timeout. The stated bar was to judge #15603 "on an observation of the shard rather than on this merge"; that bar is unchanged and unmet by this work. No closing keyword has been written anywhere, and no PR exists to carry one.

## What was verified

- Branch `claude/issue-15916-first-sibling-pays-imports` is pushed and **carries no commits** — it is identical to `origin/main` at `e581457ba`. It exists only as the landing marker for the claim above; safe to delete.
- Working tree pristine: `git status --porcelain` empty, `git diff` against base `e581457ba` empty, every instrumented file verified back at its HEAD blob hash.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` reports `this branch changes nothing against 'origin/main'` (exit 2) — the honest reading for an empty change set, not a red. No gates are owed, no changeset is owed, and `skip-changeset` is moot because nothing is proposed.

## PM ruling — LEAVE ALL FIVE, no code change. Closing as answered.

The census in this card is accurate and reproduced row for row. What settles it is the thing the card deliberately left open — *"costs are not measured per row — only the shape is"* — and the measurement went the other way from what the shape suggested.

### Every row is already outside the clock

| specifier | first-payer cost **in its own file** | same specifier in a **vacuum** |
|---|---|---|
| `./admin-user-endpoints.js` | **0.097 ms** | 591.7 ms |
| `better-auth/api` | **0.045 ms** | 215.8 ms |
| `./rate-limit-storage.js` | **0.067 ms** | 52.7 ms |
| `better-auth` | **0.082 ms** | 307.9 ms |
| `better-auth/plugins` | **0.108 ms** | 297.3 ms |
| *(sixth row, see below)* `better-auth/plugins/jwt` | **0.085 ms** | 200.7 ms |

⇒ **In every case the file's own module-top imports have already loaded that graph outside the clock.** The shape is present; the cost is already zero. Worst row is `0.108 ms` = **0.0011 %** of the 10 000 ms budget — a load tolerance of roughly **92 600×**.

⭐ **Three of the five would be actively wrong to "fix."** `admin-user-endpoints.test.ts:11`, `managed-extension-fields.test.ts:105` and `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts:103` already carry a **module-top static import of the very specifier** the `it()` body re-imports. Hoisting there would add a second module-top import of a module the file already imports. Those `await import` calls are stylistic redundancy, not a timeout hazard.

⭐ **The two single-sibling rows are answered by measurement, not by default** — which is what the dispatch asked for, since a row with no warm sibling has the shape without the observed signature. `admin-impersonate-endpoint.test.ts` (0.082 ms in-file vs 307.9 ms vacuum) and `managed-extension-fields.test.ts` (0.108 vs 297.3): leave both.

### The control is what makes the sub-millisecond readings mean something

`durability-swallow-repair.test.ts` / `./admin-import-users.js` — the site PR #15914 fixes, still unfixed on `origin/main` and therefore measurable in the same rig — read **3086.379 ms** cold with warm siblings at 0.043 and 0.034 ms. That reproduces PR #15914's independently measured 3299.6 / 0.014 ms **to within 7 %** on a shared box. ⇒ A rig that resolves 3.1 s and 0.03 ms in the same run is measuring, not returning zeros.

⭐ **And the vacuum figure for that control is the whole story of this defect family:** `./admin-import-users.js` alone costs **10 064 ms** — it **exceeds the entire 10 000 ms `testTimeout` by itself**. That is the direct, quantitative explanation for its six flakes across three cards, and it is ~28 000× the worst row this card lists.

### Coverage safety was re-established per file, not assumed

Four of the five files carry zero `vi.mock` / `vi.doMock` / `vi.resetModules` / `vi.unmock`. `auth-manager.test.ts` (4796 lines) **does** carry six `vi.mock` calls — but neither of its dynamic specifiers is among them, and both sites only destructure a function with no dependence on hook-established mock state. ⇒ A hoist there would have been safe; it is simply not worth doing.

### A sixth row the census missed, and why no card is owed for it

`better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts` / `better-auth/plugins/jwt`, first payer `it@671`, 2 sites, no explicit timeout. ⚠️ **The cause is mechanical and will recur:** that site is written with the specifier on its **own line**, so a single-line `await import(...)` regex cannot see it. The true pre-fix package total is **24 sites unmasked / 23 masked**, not 22.

⛔ No separate card, and I agree with the author's reasoning: it was measured too (0.085 ms in-file), `better-auth/plugins/jwt` is **already statically imported** at `:103`, so the verdict is identical and there is no work behind the gap. Filing a card whose entire content is "no action needed" adds a queue item and no information.

⚠️ **What is worth carrying:** the scanner lives only in a session scratchpad, so anyone re-deriving this sweep by hand will hit the same single-line-regex gap. The masking check confirmed the card's own disclosed limitation was exactly as disclosed — comment masking removes **exactly one** site (`rate-limit-storage-isolation.test.ts:128`, specifier `'x'`, in prose), taking 24→23 and the module-scope bucket 3→2 while the clocked bucket stays 21, so the finding set never contained it.

### Closing

Nothing is proposed, so nothing is owed: no changeset, no `skip-changeset` label, no gate family. `dispatch-gates.mjs` reported *"this branch changes nothing against `origin/main`"* at **exit 2** — ⛔ the honest reading for an empty change set, neither a pass nor a red, and correctly not reported as either. `check:test-typecheck` and `check-adr-0087-registration` were **NOT RUN** and are not owed on an empty diff.

⭐ The rigor that would have gone into pins went into the six measurement mutations instead: `git hash-object` deltas plus `PROBE15916` marker counts per file, anchor counts asserted against the expected occurrence count **before** writing, restores under a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths, each proven by an empty `git diff HEAD`, an empty `git status --porcelain` **and** per-file blob equality with an empty hash treated as failure. All six restored clean.

**#15603's ruling is separate and posted there.**
